patient_has_clinical_signs_of_sign_now.assessment: The patient is described as having several neurologic signs, including paratonic rigidity, myoclonic jerks, and brisk reflexes.
patient_has_clinical_signs_of_sign_now.evidence: Examination of the cranial nerves revealed clinically significant paratonic rigidity. Myoclonic jerks were seen in the arms, with symmetrically brisk reflexes.

patient_has_clinical_signs_of_sign_now@@.assessment: There is no documentation of a specific dementia diagnosis, nor a clinical impression that signs are better explained by a different type—chart does not specify or compare etiologies.

patient_has_clinical_symptoms_now.assessment: The patient is described as having multiple cognitive and behavioral symptoms: poor memory, expressive difficulties, unusual behavior, and profound functional impairment.
patient_has_clinical_symptoms_now.evidence: Progressive changes in cognition and personality; poor memory; difficulty expressing himself; unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently.

patient_has_clinical_symptoms_now@@bette.assessment: No mention of symptoms being attributable to or better explained by a different dementia type; chart is silent on comparative attribution.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_associ.assessment: Although the patient has cognitive impairment and myoclonus (which can be seen in late dementia), there is no mention of Parkinson's disease, parkinsonism, or a diagnosis of PDD.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_associ.evidence: No mention of Parkinson's disease or parkinsonism; chart documents myoclonic jerks and paratonic rigidity, but not parkinsonism.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_now.assessment: The patient meets clinical criteria for dementia: six months of progressive cognitive decline, profound functional impairment, and multiple domains affected.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_dementia_now.evidence: Six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality. He is unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_frontotemporal_.assessment: The patient displays personality and behavioral changes alongside executive dysfunction and language disturbance, which are consistent with frontotemporal dementia; clinical details are highly suggestive of FTD.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_frontotemporal_.evidence: Progressive personality change, disinhibition (undressing, pouring milk), language impairment, executive dysfunction, and myoclonus—the overall pattern is compatible with FTD.

patient_has_diagnosis_of_senile_dementia.assessment: There is no mention of fluctuating cognition, visual hallucinations, or parkinsonism features required for Lewy body dementia; the chart is silent or non-supportive for DLB.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_senile_dementia.evidence: No mention of visual hallucinations, fluctuating cognition, or parkinsonism—required for DLB diagnosis.

No evidence in the chart for either mixed dementia or specific focus on Alzheimer type with secondary vascular dementia.

patient_has_clinical_signs_of_sign_now.assessment: The patient is currently exhibiting multiple clinical signs (memory impairment, behavioral changes, paratonic rigidity, myoclonic jerks, language dysfunction) on examination.
patient_has_clinical_signs_of_sign_now.evidence: He began to have poor memory, difficulty expressing himself... He is unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently... paratonic rigidity... myoclonic jerks...

patient_has_clinical_signs_of_sign_now@@.assessment: The clinical signs reported (personality change, behavioral disinhibition, language disturbance, paratonic rigidity, myoclonus) are compatible with several dementias and not clearly better related to another non-AD dementia; paratonic rigidity and myoclonus can be seen in advanced Alzheimer's. There is no explicit evidence that another dementia type is more likely.

patient_has_finding_of_dementia_now.assessment: The patient has persistent, progressive cognitive and functional declines, fully impairing daily living, consistent with dementia.
patient_has_finding_of_dementia_now.evidence: six months of progressive changes in cognition and personality... unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently... unable to follow commands, memory loss, language disturbance

patient_has_finding_of_disability_affect.assessment: The patient currently requires help for all activities of daily living (cannot dress, bathe, toilet, or walk independently).
patient_has_finding_of_disability_affect.evidence: He is unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently

patient_has_finding_of_disease_condition.assessment: The patient currently has dementia and paratonic rigidity, both classified as diseases/conditions.
patient_has_finding_of_disease_condition.evidence: He began to have poor memory, difficulty expressing himself... paratonic rigidity... unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently...

patient_has_finding_of_disease_condition.assessment: No disease or condition is listed that would make blood sampling risky; vital signs are stable, and no mention of coagulopathy or infection.
There is no disease or condition described that casts doubt on the dementia diagnosis; findings are classic for advanced dementia.

Although behavioral disinhibition and language features could be seen in frontotemporal dementia, the chart does not clearly support a stronger alternative diagnosis over AD; evidence is not specific enough to outweigh AD.

patient_has_finding_of_drug_abuse_intheh.assessment: There is no mention of a history of drug abuse in the chart, and such a history would typically be included if present.

patient_has_finding_of_general_pathology.assessment: The patient has advanced dementia and multiple neurological findings (paratonic rigidity, myoclonic jerks, functional dependence), but these are encompassed by the dementia diagnosis and not described as a separate general pathology outside the disease focus; no broad 'other' active pathologies are described.
No condition is described that would make blood sampling risky; the abnormalities described (neurological, cognitive) do not imply unusual risk in blood draws.

patient_has_finding_of_impaired_cognitio.assessment: There is clear and repeated evidence of current cognitive impairment: the patient is disoriented, unable to spell backward, follow multistep commands, or do calculations, and has severe functional impairment.
patient_has_finding_of_impaired_cognitio.evidence: "He is unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently"; "He could not spell the word 'world' backward, could not follow commands involving multiple steps and was unable to perform simple calculations."; "He is alert and oriented to self and city but not year."

patient_has_finding_of_memory_impairment.assessment: The chart documents current memory impairment: the patient has poor memory, immediate recall but no delayed recall of words.
patient_has_finding_of_memory_impairment.evidence: "He began to have poor memory..."; "He could immediately recall three out of three words but recalled none of them after 5 minutes."

patient_has_diagnosis_of_mild_cognitive_.assessment: The patient's cognitive impairment is severe and affects daily functioning (inability to manage ADLs); thus, he does not have mild cognitive impairment but rather advanced dementia.
patient_has_diagnosis_of_mild_cognitive_.evidence: "He is unable to dress, bathe, use the toilet, or walk independently"; cognitive symptoms have progressed for 6 months and are severe.

patient_has_finding_of_symptom_now@@prov.evidence: No evidence of alternative diagnosis or contradicting features; only canonical progression of dementia described.
